assessment: The observations establish slow mixed batches and arrangement difficulties, but do not isolate selection, insertion or packing causes. One hybrid hypothesis merits a bounded test; feasibility and customer benefit remain unproved.

openings.claim: Shared shape bins may generate repeated identity-and-count reconciliation as orders change; full workshop assembly may add insertion work without reliably teaching customers partition placement. Hypothesized feedback: these organizing choices increase checking, correction and explanation demand. Replace full assembly with an order-specific mapped kit.
openings.delta: Counterfactual branch: forbid full workshop assembly. Hybrid parents are a parts-completeness witness and a placement guide: each required partition occupies a labeled outline on a packing card, and the same label identifies its location in the ordered-layout diagram. Their interaction makes one interface support packing verification and customer placement. Former assembly obligations are structural-fit checking, completeness, correct layout, stability and presentation. Replace them with reversible fit checks, a filled-card check, matched labels, a customer stability check and a restrained presentation pack; retain ordered counts, exterior color and rearrangeability.
openings.prediction: Against matched incumbent orders, mapped kits should reduce selection corrections and workshop insertion time without increasing customer placement errors. If only insertion time falls, the shared-bin feedback hypothesis lacks support. Faster packing accompanied by more customer errors rejects the proposed hybrid.
openings.probe: Use spare board for matched samples across all compartment counts; separately time selection, fit checking, assembly and packing, counting corrections. Randomly allocate the ten participants between incumbent and mapped-kit unpacking for an exploratory error comparison. Verify loaded footprint, dismantling, color and costs before adoption. The unchanged 60-unit pilot must achieve at least 59 complete orders, median workshop time at most eight minutes and at least 90% unaided arrangement; the small exploration cannot establish those rates.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: accurate order-to-parts mapping; legible removable or unobtrusive labels; correct placement diagram; reliable fit and stability checks; restraint preventing parts escaping their mapped positions; customer assembly ability.
Cards, labels, preparation and checks must fit the 500 initial and 0.40 recurring cost limits and fixed delivery date; this is unmeasured.
The sales description permits supplied unassembled partitions; customer acceptance is unmeasured.
